CONSENSUS: YES

## Final Output

Decline the requested change. This is a UI-crawl assertion failure (archive-grid affordances) on an app that already compiles and launches — exactly the shape of request that DEC-final_review11-002 and DEC-final_review12-002 already ruled out for the next scoping round. Only Claude's voice was in this discussion (Codex returned empty output again), but that voice's reasoning tracks the standing decision log exactly, with no genuine counter-position raised, so there's nothing to arbitrate — the call is to hold the line the project already drew.

**What happens instead:** this round's full scope goes to blocking item #3 — a real seed-driven renderer for at least one composition family, replacing `PlaceholderAuraRenderer` for that family, consuming the already-real `SeedEngine`/`DayStateResolver` output. This is the sole remaining item on the original three-item blocker list; items #1 and #2 are done and compiler-verified.

**Precise change scope:** implement one real composition family (e.g. painterly gradient bloom or flow-field line art) in AuraKit's renderer layer, driven by the existing seed/mood/chip inputs, wired into the debug harness / TodayScreen's existing card-display call site only (no new UI surface).

**Affected files/interfaces:** new or replaced renderer file(s) under AuraKit/Sources (data_domain-owned) implementing the actual Core Image/Metal composition; the single existing call site in TodayScreen that currently invokes `PlaceholderAuraRenderer` gets a thin swap to the new renderer. `SeedEngine`/`DayStateResolver`/persistence logic itself is not touched, only consumed.

**Forbidden-edit zones (unchanged):** project.pbxproj stays xcodegen-only; DesignSystem.swift/Theme.swift/AuraStore.swift stay primary_ui-owned with only thin call-site additions permitted; no accessibilityIdentifier wiring, ArchiveScreen changes, or any other UI-crawl-shaped edits this round; no parallel/duplicate StoreKit or export pipeline work.

**Acceptance criteria:** (1) same date+mood+chip inputs render an identical card, different days render visibly different compositions — not the same template recolored; (2) output is judged beautiful by a human reviewer, not merely "renders without crashing" or "not a flat gradient"; (3) a real, captured xcodebuild compile pass for the iOS Simulator target; (4) this round's outcome is recorded strictly as item #3 progress — it does not touch, and must not be conflated with, the archive-grid gate (which stays declined/backlogged per [REDACTED:high_entropy]) or the app's NO-GO verdict, which only the final_review phase can move.
